heard: The four lightyear pillars of creation may have already been completely destroyed. Hubble captured these towers in 1995, revealing embryonic stars forming inside dense hydrogen pockets called eggs. Nearby massive stars blast intense ultraviolet radiation and stellar winds across the gas. This photo evaporation slowly strips the gas away from each developing protostar. When an egg is uncovered, its forming star abruptly stops growing. Spitzer observations suggest a supernova shock wave wiped out the pillars 6,000 years ago. Astronomer Stephen Reynolds disputed the blast, arguing stellar winds heat the dust and erode it gradually. Because the nebula sits 7,000 light years away, telescopes must wait 1,000 years to see if we are still watching them.
